name: Valdora Supply · Order fulfilment
description: Sales orders from receipt through credit check, manager approval, picking, packing and shipping to the invoice.
planted: Approval bottleneck: three sales managers approve orders, but Marta Ilić receives 56% of them and her queue is about 2.3 times longer than her colleagues'.
From 30 Mar 2026 Jonas Berg moves to key accounts: Marta's share rises to 80% and her queue grows again, which shifts cycle time upwards.
Rework: 12% of orders are rejected at approval and updated; 8% of invoices need correcting, rising to 17% after a new price list on 4 May 2026.
Skipped and out-of-order steps: 7% of orders skip the credit check; 3% get a pro-forma invoice before picking.
Calendar: no work at weekends; the carrier collects at 15:00 on business days, and a strike cancels the pickup on 22 Apr 2026.
KPIs: in-full deliveries drop during a supplier shortage (18 May to 5 Jun 2026); emergency couriers add two one-day cost spikes (12 Mar and 10 Jun 2026).

name: Brenmoor Foods · Invoice-to-pay
description: Supplier invoices from receipt through capture, three-way match, budget-holder approval and the daily payment run.
planted: Approval batching: budget holders approve in fixed sessions. Owen Hale (47% of invoices) approves on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons only, Freya Collins on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings.
From 23 Mar 2026, to save meeting time, Owen Hale approves on Thursdays only and Freya Collins on Mondays only; Dario Russo keeps approving daily. This shifts cycle time upwards.
Overloaded specialist: Inês Duarte resolves 80% of price discrepancies and her queue is about 2.4 times longer than Tom Becker's.
Rework: 15% of matches fail and are re-matched after the discrepancy is resolved, rising to 30% after supplier price changes on 11 May 2026; 6% of approvals need a clarification first.
Skipped steps: 6% are non-PO invoices that skip matching; 3% are paid without approval.
2% of invoices are duplicates, cancelled after capture.
Calendar: no work at weekends; one payment run a day at 13:00, released to the bank at 16:30.
KPIs: supplier OTIF drops during delivery problems (2 to 20 Mar 2026); two one-day cost spikes (18 Feb and 3 Jun 2026).
